chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said:

I had a friend who was one of the scribes of the Banu Umayya, so he said to me, 'Seek permission for me from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) to see him.' So I sought permission for him, and he granted it. When he entered, he greeted and sat down, then said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I was in the office of these people, so I acquired much wealth from their worldly affairs, and I closed my eyes regarding their demands.' Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Had it not been for the Banu Umayya finding someone to write for them, collect the booty/taxes for them, fight on their behalf, and bear witness for their groups, they would not have deprived us of our rights. And if the people had left them and what is in their hands, they would not have found anything except what fell into their own hands.'

He said, 'So the youth said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Is there a way out for me from it?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If I tell you to do it, will you do it?' He said, 'I will do it.' He said to him, 'So exit from all that you acquired in their office. For whoever you recognize among them, return his wealth to him, and for whoever you do not recognize, give it in charity. And I guarantee for you, upon Allah (Exalted and Majestic), Paradise.' The youth kept his head lowered for a long time, then said, 'I have done it, may I be sacrificed for you.'

Ibn Abu Hamza said, 'So the youth returned with us to Kufa, and he did not leave anything upon the face of the earth except that he extracted from it, even his clothes that were on his body.' He said, 'So I apportioned a share for him, and we bought him clothes and sent him expenses.' He said, 'And not many months passed until he fell ill, and we used to visit him.' He said, 'So I entered upon him one day and he was in the transit (of death). He opened his eyes, then said to me, 'O Ali! By Allah, your Master kept his promise to me.' Then he died.

So we took care of his affairs, and I went out until I entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). When he looked at me, he said, 'O Ali! By Allah, we kept our promise to your companion.' I said, 'You have spoken the truth, may I be sacrificed for you! By Allah, this is how he said to me at the time of his death.'

key_terms.السَّوْق: Transit or the process of dying

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wealth acquired by officials in the Umayyad government according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the concept of 'ghulul' (extraction of wealth) within the Umayyad bureaucracy, where the Imam emphasizes that their power relied on the administrative and military services of their scribes. The Imam’s instruction to liquidate all assets—even clothing—demonstrates a rigorous standard of total divestment to ensure purity of faith, a practice validated by the Imam’s posthumous confirmation of the scribe's fidelity. This narrative underscores the Shia scholarly view that serving unjust rulers requires careful separation of worldly gain from spiritual integrity.
